instruction: Some websites use custom fonts that make text hard to read for me. Could you disable custom fonts in Chrome so all websites use only the standard system fonts?

metadata.explanation: Task requires disabling custom fonts from websites. The evaluator checks if the disable_fonts_enabled setting is true. When enabled, this prevents websites from using custom web fonts and forces them to use only the system's standard fonts.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the Chrome Preferences file setting 'webkit.webprefs.fonts_disabled' which controls custom font disabling
Metric correctly compares the boolean value against expected 'true'
Postconfig appropriately restarts Chrome to ensure settings are persisted to disk before verification
Expected value is semantically correct (true = custom fonts disabled)
Complete coverage: evaluator checks the exact requirement from the instruction (disable custom fonts)
Data flow is correct: instruction requirement → getter extracts correct state → metric compares correctly
Runtime feasible: handles multiple platforms (Windows/Mac/Linux) with correct Preferences file paths
Error handling is conservative (returns False on failure)
